title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 212
paragraphs: During these assaults it is said that the king, looking on, leapt up from his seat three times, struck with fear for his army. So they fought that day. On the following day the barbarians fared no better: because the men opposing them were few, they engaged in the expectation that the Greeks would be found disabled and no longer capable of raising their hands in battle against them. But the Greeks were drawn up by companies as well as by nationalities, and they fought in turn, each in succession — except for the Phokians, who were posted on the mountain to guard the path. So the Persians, finding nothing different from what they had met the day before, withdrew from the fight.
